# Lab 12.25: Enable DNSSEC & a Response Policy

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on DNSSEC for a public zone, then use a Cloud DNS response policy to block a malicious domain inside your VPC.

## Steps

1. **Create a public zone with DNSSEC.** Use a domain or subdomain you own.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dns managed-zones create lab-public \
  --dns-name="lab.YOUR_DOMAIN." \
  --description="DNSSEC lab" \
  --dnssec-state=on</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Get the DS record.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dns dns-keys list --zone=lab-public \
  --filter="type=keySigning" --format="value(ds_record())"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Add this DS record at your registrar, or in the parent zone. Without it the chain of trust is not complete.

3. **Check DNSSEC.** After the DS record is published, test with `dig +dnssec lab.YOUR_DOMAIN SOA`. The answer includes `RRSIG` records.

4. **Create a response policy for the VPC.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dns response-policies create lab-rp \
  --networks=default --description="Block bad domains"

gcloud dns response-policies rules create block-bad \
  --response-policy=lab-rp \
  --dns-name="malware.example.com." \
  --local-data=name="malware.example.com.",type="A",ttl=300,rrdatas="0.0.0.0"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Turn on DNS query logging.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dns policies create dns-logging --networks=default \
  --enable-logging --description="Log DNS queries"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **Test from a VM** in the `default` network.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute ssh ANY_VM --zone=us-central1-a --tunnel-through-iap \
  --command="getent hosts malware.example.com"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   It resolves to `0.0.0.0`. In **Logs Explorer**, filter `resource.type="dns_query"` to see the query.

7. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dns response-policies rules delete block-bad --response-policy=lab-rp
gcloud dns response-policies update lab-rp --networks=""
gcloud dns response-policies delete lab-rp
gcloud dns policies update dns-logging --networks=""
gcloud dns policies delete dns-logging
gcloud dns managed-zones update lab-public --dnssec-state=off
gcloud dns managed-zones delete lab-public</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Remove the DS record at the registrar before turning DNSSEC off on a live domain.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| DNSSEC | Signed answers, needs the DS record at the parent |
| Response policy | Overrides answers for chosen names in the VPC |
| Blocked domain | Resolves to `0.0.0.0` |
| Query logs | Help detect malware lookups |
